Create a basic interactive table using DT

Source: R/table_basic_interactive.R
table_basic_interactive.Rd

Interactive counterpart of table_basic() for HTML output: shows a data frame as a searchable, paged DT table with a filter box above each column and no row-number column. Useful for long tables (e.g. data-cleaning QC tables) that are too long to print in full.

Usage

table_basic_interactive(
  d,
  page_length = 10,
  use_column_labels = TRUE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

d

data.frame. Dataset to display as a table.

page_length

numeric(1). Number of rows shown per page. Must be a positive whole number. Default is 10.

use_column_labels

logical(1). If TRUE (default), use the label attribute of columns as headers where available (e.g. set with labelled::var_label()), otherwise use column names.

filter

character(1). Where to show the column filters: "top" (default), "bottom" or "none". Passed to DT::datatable(filter = ...).

options

list. DataTables options (see https://rstudio.github.io/DT/options.html), merged with the defaults list(pageLength = page_length, autoWidth = TRUE): options given here are added, or replace a default of the same name. For example, list(lengthMenu = c(5, 10, 20)) adds a menu for changing the page length.

...

Further arguments passed to DT::datatable(), e.g. caption, class (e.g. "cell-border stripe"), style or extensions. data, colnames and rownames are set by this function and cannot be passed.

Value

A datatables htmlwidget. It can be piped into DT's formatting functions, such as DT::formatRound() or DT::formatStyle().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol"),
  age = c(25.12, 30.55, 35.91)
)
attr(df$age, "label") <- "Age, years"

table_basic_interactive(df)



# Show 2 rows per page and use column names as headers
table_basic_interactive(df, page_length = 2, use_column_labels = FALSE)



# No column filters, a page-length menu and a styled table with a caption
table_basic_interactive(
  df,
  filter = "none",
  options = list(lengthMenu = c(2, 5, 10)),
  class = "cell-border stripe",
  caption = "Participants"
)



# Round a column with DT's formatting functions
table_basic_interactive(df) |>
  DT::formatRound("age", digits = 1)
